reasoning: The proposal is nearly identical to "Prompt Attacks Reveal Superficial Knowledge Removal in Unlearning Methods" (arXiv 2506.10236, OpenReview RvwYQ4RycZ), which implements a battery of surface-form-preserving prompt transformations (rephrase as conversation/poem, translate to another language, remove technical terms, replace terms with variables, filler text, multiple-choice and free-form), applies them to WMDP against eight unlearning methods across three model families plus reference models, all inference-only, and explicitly measures whether unlearned models genuinely remove vs. merely suppress hazardous knowledge — exactly the proposal's research question and "suppression gap" framing (best-over-transformations accuracy vs. default accuracy). The same problem is independently corroborated by "Towards Robust Evaluation of Unlearning in LLMs via Data Transformations" (2411.15477) and "An Adversarial Perspective on Machine Unlearning for AI Safety" (2409.18025), which show RMU-style unlearning obfuscates rather than removes knowledge recoverable via prompt manipulation. The only marginal delta is packaging this as a single standardized metric, which is not enough to lift it above already_solved given 2506.10236 already reports format/transformation accuracy gaps on WMDP.

evidence.title: Prompt Attacks Reveal Superficial Knowledge Removal in Unlearning Methods
evidence.summary: Directly addresses the proposal's question and method: a battery of prompt transformations (rephrase as conversation/poem, translate to another language, remove/replace technical terms, filler text, multiple-choice vs free-form) applied to WMDP against 8 unlearning methods across 3 model families, inference-only, to distinguish genuine removal from superficial output suppression. Uses output-based, logit-based, and probe analysis; reports accuracy recovery (e.g., Hindi filler recovers 57.3% on ELM). This is essentially the proposed Prompt-Attack Probe Battery and suppression-gap metric.

evidence.title: Towards Robust Evaluation of Unlearning in LLMs via Data Transformations
evidence.summary: Proposes evaluating unlearning robustness by applying data/format transformations to probe whether 'forgotten' knowledge resurfaces, finding performance gaps across formats and arguing multiple formats are needed for reliable evaluation. Establishes the transformation-based evaluation paradigm the proposal relies on.

evidence.title: An Adversarial Perspective on Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
evidence.summary: Shows that unlearning methods like RMU obfuscate rather than remove hazardous knowledge, with capabilities recoverable via prompting/adaptive strategies on WMDP — directly supporting the suppression-vs-removal distinction the proposal aims to quantify.

evidence.title: Unlearning Isn't Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
evidence.summary: Demonstrates that supposedly unlearned knowledge is recoverable (weight perturbations near output layer recover tokens), reinforcing that the suppression-vs-removal problem is already established and studied in the literature.

evidence.title: Position: LLM Unlearning Benchmarks are Weak Measures of Progress
evidence.summary: Argues current unlearning benchmarks/evaluations conflate suppression with removal and are weak measures of true forgetting, the exact gap the proposal claims to address — but this critique and remedies are already published.
